subject.title: fix(message): ignore populated Telegram location on model sends

question: Should model-tool-originated Telegram sends be the sole trusted origin allowed to discard a populated location when real content is present, while direct and API requests remain strictly rejected?
rationale: This is an intentional trust and compatibility boundary, not a mechanical test gap: the repository needs owner confirmation that the origin signal is server-controlled and that the asymmetric behavior is the desired public contract.

options.title: Confirm the private origin boundary
options.body: Approve the bounded model-tool-only normalization after verifying that ordinary Gateway/API callers cannot supply the trusted origin.

options.title: Keep all populated locations strict
options.body: Reject this compatibility exception and require model clients to stop emitting location objects alongside content.

options.title: Pause for a different public contract
options.body: Defer the PR if maintainers want a broader channel or message-action policy rather than a Telegram-specific repair.

recommendation.title: Confirm the private origin boundary
recommendation.body: Approve the bounded model-tool-only normalization after verifying that ordinary Gateway/API callers cannot supply the trusted origin.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the adjacent merged location-normalization behavior and are the strongest evidence-backed routing candidate in the supplied history.
